1  JUDGMENT

The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed by the claimant in M.C.O.P.No.344 of 2008,
aggrieved over the quantum of compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, II Small Causes Court, Chennai, wherein, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,01,800/- as compensation for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident taken place on 18.07.2007.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, II Small Causes Court, Chennai
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties are referred to hereunder according to status and ranking before the trial Court.

3. On 18.07.2007 at about 8.00 a.m., the claimant was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.TN 29 4357 from Kaveripattinam to Kalvehalli to his house on KRP Dam Road, near Perumal Temple on the left side of the road, at that time, the driver of the Pickup Van, bearing https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis registration No.KA 01/AB 8000 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained fracture on his right knee and also sustained multiple injuries all over his body.
A case was registered by the Kaveripattinam Police against the driver of the Pickup Van in Crime No.727/2007 under Sections 279, 337 IPC.

Hence, the petitioner claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.5,00,000/-.
4.
The first respondent - vehicle owner, remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

The second respondent is the Insurance Company countered that the accident was occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the claimant and that the driver of the Pickup van is not responsible for the accident.

They have also disputed the contributory negligence only on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and negligence injuries and disabilities caused to the petitioner and stated that compensation claimed before the Tribunal is on the higher side and prays to dismiss the Claim Petition.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

Before the Tribunal, the claimant was examined as P.W.1 and one Dr.Ashok Kumar was examined as P.W.2 to prove the disability and claimant marked documents as Exs.A1 to A10 and on the side of the second respondent-Insurance Company no witness was examined and no documents marked.

6. Based on the evidence adduced before the Tribunal, it is held that from the evidence of the injured and since no rebuttal evidence adduced by the respondent side to disprove the evidence of the claimant, the rash and the negligent act of the driver of the private bus is responsible for the injuries caused to the claimant.

7. The Tribunal has awarded compensation on the following heads: Permanent Disability at Rs.40,000/-; Compensation of Pain and Sufferings and mental agony at Rs.10,000/-; Partial Loss of earning capacity at Rs.9,000/-; Transport to Hospital and Extra Nourishment at Rs.5,000/-;
Medical Expenses at Rs.35,776.36/-; and Attendant Expenses at Rs.2,000/-.
Kanagaraj vs Mohan Kumar on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67647768/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8.
The claimant has filed this appeal on the grievance that the compensation awarded for the injures and disabilities caused to him is on lower side and prays to increase the compensation.

9. The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the claimant has suffered 40% injury and the Tribunal has followed the percentage method and granted Rs.1,000/- per percentage of injury sustained by him, which is on the lower side.
Similarly, in other heads also the compensation granted needs to be revised.
He has also listed out further complications of the injuries sustained by him.
11. The Tribunal after considering the evidence of P.W.2 and medical records has accepted the percentage fixed by the P.W.2 i.e., 40%.

The claimant has not sustained any permanent functional disability in view of the injuries sustained by him by following the Judgements of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar vs. Ajaykumar reported in 2011 1 SCC 343.

entities.text: Rajkumar vs. Ajaykumar reported in 2011 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the injuries sustained by the claimant is not the functional permanent disability, granting of compensation by adopting percentage method is proper.
The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.1,000/- per percentage of disability.
Admittedly, the accident was occurred on 18.07.2007, and during that relevant period the Courts have adopted granting of Rs.2,000/- per percentage of injury.
Accordingly, I am inclined to enhance the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation for a sum of Rs.2,000/- per percentage of disability.

Accordingly, compensation awarded under the head permanent disability is enhanced to Rs.2,000/- per percentage and the appellant is entitled for a sum of Rs.80,000/- [Rs.2000 X 40% = Rs.80,000/-] under the head Permanent Disability.
12. The Tribunal has also granted compensation for a sum of Rs.10,000/-for pain and sufferings and mental agony and this Court finds that the same is fair and proper.

The injured was admitted into the hospital and undergone in-patient treatment on 18.07.2007 and discharged on 23.07.2007 as Kanagaraj vs Mohan Kumar on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67647768/
3 per Ex.A4-Discharge Summary shows that the claimant was fitted with L-plates and screws on the right tibial Condyles.

entities.text: Kanagaraj vs Mohan Kumar on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the period of taking in-patient treatment, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.9,000/- as partial loss of earning during the treatment period and the same is confirmed.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- for Transport to Hospital and Extra Nourishment and the same is on the lower side and this Court enhance the amount to Rs.10,000/-
for transport to Hospital and Extra Nourishment.
The Tribunal has allowed the entire medical expenses of Rs.35,776.36/- and this Court is of the view that no https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis need for further revision in this particular head.
The Tribunal has awarded attendant charges for a sum of Rs.2,000/- but failed to grant future medical expenses.
Admittedly, the claimant has fitted with L-plates, screws which requires to be removed, subsequently.
Accordingly, I am inclined to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head future medical expenses.

13. Accordingly, the award passed by the Tribunal under various heads are hereby enhanced is as follows:

Transport to Rs.5,000/- Rs.10,000/- Enhanced Hospital and Extra Nourishment

5. Medical expenses Rs.35,776.36/- Rs.35,776.36/- Confirmed 6. Attendant Rs.2,000/- Rs.2,000/- Confirmed Expenses 7 . F u t u r e M e d i c a l . . . . . . R s . 1 5 , 0 0 0 / - G r a n t e d E x p e n s e s https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Total Rs.1,01,776.36/ Rs.1,61,776.36/ Enhanced by - - Rs.60,000/-
14.

In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is at Rs.1,01,776.36/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.1,61,776.36/- [Rupees One Lakh Sixty One Thousand Seven Hundred and Seventy Six and Thirty Six Paise only] together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of Claim Petition till the date of deposit.

The second respondent/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount, now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.344 of 2008,
on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Additional Subordinate Judge, Krishnagiri.

On such deposit, the appellant/claimant is entitled to withdraw the amount, now awarded by this Court Kanagaraj vs Mohan Kumar on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67647768/
4 along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn without making any formal application.
Since this Court has enhanced the compensation, the appellant/claimant is directed to pay necessary Court fee, if any, on the enhanced compensation.
In other aspects, the award of the Tribunal shall stand confirmed.
There shall be no order as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis to costs in the present appeal.
